mainTopic: Carrying in a ship and in an אכסדרה: the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל, and the גזירות that keep roofs, courtyards and קרפפות separate.
overview: The amud opens with the end of the מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about carrying in a ספינה. רב says one may carry in the whole ship because it has walls. שמואל says only four אמות, because the walls are only meant to keep water out. שמואל himself rules that the הלכה follows רב, though רב agrees about a ship that was turned over to be tarred. רב אחא בריה דרבא says שמואל's ruling was really said about a different case: an אכסדרה standing in a field. רב and שמואל argue there about whether פי תקרה יורד וסותם applies. The גמרא then challenges each side. The challenge to רב, who follows רבי מאיר, is answered with the גזירה of רב יצחק בר אבדימי. The challenge to שמואל, who follows the רבנן, is answered with a גזירה in case the roof shrinks, which is noticeable for a קרפף but not for a roof. Finally, רב יהודה begins listing the domains according to רבי מאיר, and his list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רב's reason: the ship has walls
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the last words of רב's ruling: one may carry in the whole ship because it has walls.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רב's statement from the previous lines. He permits carrying throughout a ship because the ship's sides count as real walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רב, the ship's sides work as מחיצות that turn the ship into a private, enclosed area. That is why one may carry anywhere inside it, not just within four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: partitions or walls that enclose an area

phrases.english: since there are partitions.
phrases.notes: Conclusion of רב's reasoning, which began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's ruling, which started earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: one may carry throughout a ship, because its sides are valid מחיצות.

steps.title: שמואל: only four cubits, since the walls keep out water
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that one may carry only four אמות in a ship, because its walls are made to keep water out, not to form a home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: One may carry in it only within four אמות, because the walls were made to keep water out.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says the ship's walls do not count as real walls for carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the ship physically has sides. They argue about what those sides are for. שמואל says walls built to keep out water are not walls that create a living space, so the ship is treated like open space where one may carry only four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: four cubits, the small area where carrying is always allowed
to chase away or keep out water

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not deny that the ship has sides. His point is that the purpose of the sides (keeping out water) stops them from counting as halachic walls.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
one may not carry in it
except within four cubits —
the partitions are made to keep water out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: carrying in a ship is limited to four אמות, because its walls are only meant to keep water out.

steps.title: Asking שמואל which view is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר יוסף asks שמואל whether the הלכה follows שמואל or רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר יוסף said to שמואל: Is the הלכה like you, or is the הלכה like רב?
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks שמואל directly how we rule in practice. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack on שמואל's logic. It only asks for the practical ruling between two opposing views.

keyTerms.meaning: like you, in line with your view

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף לִשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Yosef said to Shmuel:
Is the halacha like you
or is the halacha like Rav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical ruling on the מחלוקת just presented.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view is the practical הלכה: רב's or שמואל's?

steps.title: שמואל answers: the הלכה follows רב
steps.stepSummary: שמואל himself rules that the הלכה follows רב, his own opponent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The הלכה is like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל admits that in practice we follow רב, so one may carry throughout the ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is unusual for a sage to rule against his own view. It shows that שמואל found רב's reasoning, that the sides are real walls, more convincing for practical הלכה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי's version, the practical הלכה is that one may carry throughout an upright ship, following רב, and even שמואל agrees to this ruling. Step 9 brings another version that places this ruling on the אכסדרה instead.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical ruling. The rest of this passage then marks out where even רב would limit carrying.

phrases.english: He said to him: The halacha is like Rav.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רב: one may carry throughout the ship.

steps.title: רב agrees about an overturned ship
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל, quoting רב חייא בר יוסף, reports that רב admits that if the ship was turned upside down, one may carry on it only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב חייא בר יוסף: And רב agrees that if one turned the ship over onto its mouth, one may carry on it only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limits רב's ruling. In the case of an overturned ship, רב agrees with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב's walls made the whole ship carryable. Now we learn of a case where the same ship does not get that status. We do not yet know why, and the next steps work that out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav Chiyya bar Yosef:
And Rav concedes
that if one overturned it onto its mouth,
that one may not carry on it
except within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַב שֶׁאִם כְּפָאָהּ עַל פִּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רב's ruling, which was just accepted as הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רב limits carrying to four אמות on an overturned ship.

steps.title: Why was the ship turned over?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for what purpose the ship was overturned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He overturned it — for what purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the case in רב's concession. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the ship was overturned decides whether it counts as a living space. So the גמרא has to pin down the purpose before the concession makes sense.

phrases.english: He overturned it — for what purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the case described in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the purpose of turning the ship over?

steps.title: Not for living under it, which would match a lone roof
steps.stepSummary: If the ship was turned over to live under it, it would be no different from a גג יחידי, where רב permits carrying. So that cannot be the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he turned it over to live under it, how is it different from a single, isolated roof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible reason and rejects it. Living under the ship would make it like a גג יחידי, where רב allows carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק, רב permits carrying on a גג יחידי, an isolated roof over a home. An overturned ship used for living under is just like that roof. So רב should permit carrying there, and his concession cannot be about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say, if we suggest

phrases.english: If you say it was to live under it,
what is different from an isolated roof?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא לָדוּר תַּחְתֶּיהָ מַאי שְׁנָא מִגַּג יְחִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes one answer to the question in step 6 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects explaining רב's concession as a ship overturned for living under.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is the same as a גג יחידי, where רב permits carrying, so רב would not limit it.

steps.title: It was turned over to coat it with tar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב's concession is about a ship turned over to be tarred, not to be lived in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he turned it over to tar it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct case: the ship was flipped only to coat its bottom with tar. In that case it is not a living space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ship flipped for repair work is not a home, so its sides are not walls that make a residence. That is why even רב limits carrying to four אמות there, while he permits carrying in a גג יחידי or an upright ship.
steps.whatToRemember: רב permits carrying in an upright ship because of its walls, and the הלכה follows him. He agrees it is only four אמות when the ship is overturned to be tarred, because then it is not a living space.

phrases.english: Rather, where he overturned it to tar it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case of step 7 with the correct one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ship was overturned to live under it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ship was overturned to tar it, so it is not a residence and carrying is limited to four אמות.

steps.title: Two versions of where the teaching belongs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches the previous discussion about the ship. רב אחא בריה דרבא teaches it about an אכסדרה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי teaches it about a ship, and רב אחא son of רבא teaches it about a portico.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that two אמוראים disagree about which case the earlier teaching was said on. This line sets up the next step, which explains the portico case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ראשונים (ריטב"א), the teaching here is שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רב. רב אשי says it was said about the ship, as we just learned. רב אחא בריה דרבא says it was really said about a different argument between רב and שמואל, the one about an אכסדרה.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches it (he places this teaching on a certain case)
A portico: a roofed structure with no walls or incomplete walls

phrases.english: Rav Ashi teaches it regarding a ship,
and Rav Acha, son of Rava,
teaches it regarding a portico.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of which case the earlier teaching applies to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditions about the teaching's location: the ship, or the אכסדרה.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about a portico in a field
steps.stepSummary: About an אכסדרה standing in a בקעה, רב allows carrying in all of it. שמואל allows carrying only within four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was said: about a portico in a field, רב says one may carry in all of it. שמואל says one may carry in it only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the argument between רב and שמואל about the portico. This is the argument that רב אחא's version refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה has a roof but no real walls. Standing in an open field, which is a כרמלית, the question is whether it counts as a closed private area. רב treats it as fully enclosed. שמואל does not, so he limits carrying to four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was said (an אמוראic dispute is quoted)
An open field or valley (a כרמלית)

phrases.english: As it was stated: a portico in a field.
Rav said: it is permitted to carry throughout all of it,
and Shmuel said: one may not carry in it
except within four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the dispute that רב אחא's version refers to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: one may carry in the whole אכסדרה. שמואל: only within four אמות.

steps.title: The reason: does the roof edge count as a wall?
steps.stepSummary: רב holds פי תקרה יורד וסותם, so the roof edge acts as walls. שמואל does not hold this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says one may carry in all of it, because we say the edge of the roof comes down and closes it in. שמואל says only four אמות, because we do not say the edge of the roof comes down and closes it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats both opinions and gives the reason behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument depends on one idea. Does the edge of the roof count as if it came down to the ground and made walls? רב says yes, so the portico is a closed private area. שמואל says no, so it stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge of the roof is seen as coming down and closing the sides like a wall

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between רב and שמואל about the אכסדרה comes down to פי תקרה יורד וסותם. רב uses it and שמואל does not.

phrases.english: Rav said: it is permitted to carry throughout all of it,
since we say: the edge of the roof descends and seals.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בָּהּ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע —
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: one may carry in it only within four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם.
phrases.english: since we do not say: the edge of the roof descends and seals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument depends on whether פי תקרה יורד וסותם applies.

steps.title: Challenge to רב: why not carry from roof to courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: If רב follows רבי מאיר, who treats roofs as one domain, carrying from a roof to a courtyard should also be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב, who follows רבי מאיר: let one carry from a roof to a courtyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. It argues that his opinion, based on רבי מאיר, should lead to allowing something that רבי מאיר forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב's opinion was linked to רבי מאיר, who allows carrying between roofs. A roof and a courtyard are both private areas. So why does רבי מאיר keep them apart and forbid carrying between them?

phrases.english: But Rav, according to Rabbi Meir,
let one carry from a roof to a courtyard?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, לִיטַּלְטְלֵי מִגַּג לְחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב's opinion, linked to רבי מאיר, against רבי מאיר's ruling that a roof and a courtyard are separate.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's opinion, which follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both a roof and a courtyard are private areas. So by רבי מאיר's logic, carrying between them should be allowed, yet he forbids it.

steps.title: Answer: a decree because of רב יצחק בר אבדימי
steps.stepSummary: Carrying from a roof to a courtyard is forbidden only because of a rabbinic גזירה, based on רב יצחק בר אבדימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, because of the teaching of רב יצחק בר אבדימי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that by Torah law this would really be allowed. רבי מאיר forbade it as a protective decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר אבדימי taught a decree against moving things between two separate high areas, even if both have the same status. The concern is that people might come to do a Torah-level violation. So the ban is a protective fence, not a contradiction of רבי מאיר's basic view.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי.
phrases.english: It is a decree because of the teaching of Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: The ban is explained as a rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a roof and a courtyard are both private, carrying between them should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it is allowed. It is forbidden because of the decree of רב יצחק בר אבדימי.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: why not carry from roof to enclosure?
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל follows the רבנן, a large isolated roof is a כרמלית like a קרפף, so carrying between them should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל, who follows the רבנן: let one carry from a roof to an enclosure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a matching challenge against שמואל's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, an isolated roof (larger than two בית סאה) has the status of a כרמלית. A קרפף is also a כרמלית. So why do the רבנן forbid carrying between a roof and a קרפף?

keyTerms.meaning: A fenced enclosure, not made for living in

phrases.english: And Shmuel, according to the Rabbis,
let one carry from a roof to an enclosure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אַלִּיבָּא דְרַבָּנַן, נִיטַּלְטֵל מִגַּג לְקַרְפֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the challenge to רב, now aimed at שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's opinion, which follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A roof and a קרפף are both כרמלית, so carrying between them should be allowed. Yet the רבנן forbid it.

steps.title: Answer: a decree in case the roof shrinks
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא explains that it is forbidden because of a גזירה: the roof might become smaller and turn into a private domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר עולא said: it is a decree, in case the roof becomes smaller.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר עולא answers the challenge against שמואל with another protective decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the roof became smaller than two בית סאה, it would become a private domain. Carrying from a private domain to a קרפף is forbidden. So the רבנן banned carrying from any roof to a קרפף, to avoid that mistake.
steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges are answered the same way. Carrying between areas of the same status can still be forbidden because of a rabbinic גזירה.

phrases.english: Rava bar Ulla said:
It is a decree, lest the roof become diminished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִפָּחֵת הַגָּג
steps.terutzResolutionType: The ban is explained as a rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a roof and a קרפף are both כרמלית, carrying between them should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden by decree, in case the roof shrinks and becomes a private domain.

steps.title: Then carrying between two enclosures should also be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If we worry that a roof might shrink, we should also worry that a קרפף might shrink, and forbid carrying from one קרפף to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a person should also not carry from one קרפף to another קרפף, because perhaps one of them will shrink, and he will come to carry anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of רבא בר עולא from step 15. It says his worry should apply to two קרפפות as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר עולא said that carrying between a large roof and a קרפף is forbidden because the roof might shrink and become a רשות היחיד. A קרפף can also shrink in the same way. Yet carrying between two קרפפות is allowed, so his reasoning seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: A large enclosed area that was not fenced in for living purposes, such as a storage yard
If so; this opens a challenge based on the previous answer

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: Refers to רבא בר עולא's גזירה that the roof might shrink.

phrases.english: from one enclosure to another enclosure
he also should not carry,
perhaps it will shrink
phrases.notes: One קרפף might become small enough to count as a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: and he will come to carry anyway?
phrases.notes: He would keep carrying out of habit, even after the status changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מִקַּרְפֵּף לְקַרְפֵּף נָמֵי לָא יְטַלְטֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 15 by applying its logic to a parallel case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר עולא's גזירה that a roof might shrink and become a רשות היחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same shrinking worry applies to a קרפף, yet carrying between two קרפפות is allowed. So the worry cannot be the real reason.

steps.title: A shrinking enclosure is noticeable, but a shrinking roof is not
steps.stepSummary: A קרפף has walls, so if it shrinks people will see it. A roof has no walls, so if it shrinks nobody will notice.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a קרפף, if it shrinks the matter is noticeable. Here, with a roof, if it shrinks the matter is not noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא בר עולא's גזירה. It explains why the worry applies to a roof but not to a קרפף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה is only needed when people might not realize the situation has changed. When a קרפף shrinks, its walls are moved and everyone sees it, so nobody will carry by mistake. A roof has no real walls, so a change in its size goes unnoticed, and people might keep carrying wrongly.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here; used to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The roof-to-קרפף ban stands, because a roof's change in size is not visible, while a קרפף's change is.

phrases.english: There, if it shrinks,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of a קרפף.

phrases.english: the matter is noticeable.
Here, if it shrinks,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case of a roof.

phrases.english: the matter is not noticeable.
phrases.notes: A roof has no walls to show the change.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, אִי מִיפְּחִית מִינַּכְרָא לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) based on how visible the change is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קרפף and a roof are the same, since both can shrink, so both should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a roof needs the גזירה, because its shrinking is not noticeable. A קרפף's shrinking is obvious because of its walls.

steps.title: רב יהודה begins his summary of the domains according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה states that according to רבי מאיר, all roofs together are one separate domain, and all courtyards together are another separate domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: When you look carefully, you will find that according to רבי מאיר, roofs are a domain of their own, and courtyards are a domain of their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב יהודה. It sums up how the different areas are grouped according to רבי מאיר. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a person may carry from one roof to another roof, because all roofs count as one domain. In the same way, a person may carry from one courtyard to another courtyard. But roofs and courtyards are separate groups, so carrying between a roof and a courtyard is not allowed (as step 13 explained, this is because of a rabbinic גזירה).

keyTerms.meaning: When you look into it, you will find you can say; it introduces a careful summary
A domain of their own; a separate group within which carrying is allowed

steps.confusionAlert: "A domain of their own" does not mean each roof is separate. It means all the roofs together form one group. You may carry within that group, but not into a different group such as courtyards.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
When you look carefully, you will find you can say,
according to the words of Rabbi Meir
roofs are a domain of their own,
phrases.notes: One may carry from roof to roof.

phrases.english: courtyards are a domain of their own,
phrases.notes: One may carry from courtyard to courtyard. The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כְּשֶׁתִּמְצָא לוֹמַר, לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the back-and-forth about רב and שמואל, the גמרא opens a summary of the domains according to רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, roofs form one separate domain and courtyards form another separate domain, and carrying is allowed within each group. The list continues on the next amud.
